_note: Per-message first-availability latency, ~5h wall. Six incremental cells mint a fresh key every 60s (adv 1s => ~60 broadcasts per key), so every key is one independent 'message'. detections_before_remove=1 drops each key the instant its first report lands, so first_fetched_at-send_time is one clean send->retrievable latency sample per key and the queue holds only still-in-flight keys (well under queue_soft_cap, so the adaptive timeout does not prematurely drop propagating keys). ~282 attempted keys => a real distribution + tail, not 8 correlated soaks. A key never observed within its window times out at lost_timeout_s=900 (a deliverability miss, not a latency sample). Timing: 6 x 2820s transmission (16920s) + up to 900s final drain + one-time flash ~= 5h. Latency comes from this live poller BY DESIGN; deliverability must still come from the offline resweep: analyze.py results/<run> --deliver-window-s 900. Tunables: shorten update_interval_ms for more (but lower-pickup) keys; raise it for higher per-key pickup.
